body:
If your state taxes vaping products, the tax can change what you pay in a way that is easy to miss when you compare prices. Some states add a large percentage, some charge by the milliliter and some do not tax vapor products at all, so the same bottle or device can cost noticeably different amounts in different places. This guide explains why states tax vapor products, the main ways the tax is calculated, how online sales and the PACT Act fit in, how taxes show on an order with us, how the free-shipping threshold is measured, how to find exact figures for your state and how to compare real costs. It is general information, not legal advice. Laws change and differ by state and city, so check the rules where you live. Everything we sell is for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Why states tax vapes
Many states levy excise taxes on e-cigarettes and e-liquids, similar to those on cigarettes. The goals vary. Some states want revenue, some want to discourage use, and some want to treat vapor products like other tobacco products for consistency. Because each state decides for itself, there is no single national vapor tax, and rates and methods differ widely. A few states have no specific vapor tax, while others charge rates that can double the price of a device.

## How taxes are calculated
Methods differ, and you may find more than one in a single state.

- **Percentage of price:** a share of the wholesale price or the retail price. A higher price means more tax, so premium devices cost more tax than economy ones.
- **Per milliliter:** a fixed amount for each milliliter of liquid. Larger bottles carry more tax, but the tax per milliliter stays the same.
- **Per device or per cartridge:** a flat amount per item, whatever its price.
- **Mixed systems:** a combination, such as a percentage on devices and a per-milliliter rate on liquids.
- **Different treatment of open and closed systems:** some states tax pre-filled disposables differently from refillable systems and bottles.

Because of those differences, you cannot guess a tax from the price alone. A $15 disposable and a $15 bottle can carry different amounts.

## Online sales and the PACT Act
Under the PACT Act, remote sellers must comply with state tax requirements, and in some cases collect and remit them. That means that when you buy online, a seller that follows the law handles the tax for the state where you live, or reports the sale to the state. See the [PACT Act overview](/blog/pact-act-explained-for-vape-buyers/). Some sellers cannot ship to certain states at all because the requirements are too complex, which is one reason availability differs by place. See [where we ship and where we do not](/blog/where-we-ship-and-where-we-do-not/).

## Seeing it on your order
Where a tax applies to an order, it is itemized in your order total, so you see it before you pay. Free-shipping thresholds are measured before tax, so tax does not push you over or under the line. Our free shipping applies to orders of $200 or more after discount and before tax. See [minimum order and free shipping explained](/blog/minimum-order-and-free-shipping-explained/). If you are unsure what a line on your summary means, contact us before you pay.

## Where to get exact numbers
Rates change often, and the exact rules depend on the product type and your location. Check your state's department of revenue or taxation website for current rules, and search for "vapor product tax" or "e-cigarette tax" with your state's name. Look at the date of any page you use, because older pages may be out of date. Some cities and counties add their own taxes on top of the state's. Official sources are more reliable than summaries on social media or in forums.

## Impact on prices
Tax can raise the cost of a vape noticeably in some states. A device that looks cheap before tax can cost much more after it, and a larger bottle can carry a larger tax even if the price per milliliter is low. When you compare costs between products or between sellers, compare the final total, including tax and shipping, not just the sticker price. Compare overall costs with [cost per puff](/blog/how-to-compare-vape-prices-per-puff/), and remember that bulk purchases can lower both shipping and cost per item. See [bulk buying tips](/blog/bulk-buying-vapes-save-money/).

### A worked example with round numbers
Suppose a state charges a 20% tax on the retail price of vapor products. A $20 disposable would carry $4.00 of tax, for $24.00. A $100 order of mixed products would carry $20.00, for $120.00. If your state instead charged $0.10 per milliliter of liquid, a 30 mL bottle would carry $3.00, and a 100 mL bottle $10.00, regardless of the sticker price. These figures are only illustrations. The actual rate for your state is on your state's website, and any tax that applies is shown in your order summary before you pay.

## Taxes and the 10% discount
The 10% discount for cryptocurrency and gift cards applies to the product subtotal. How tax interacts with a discount depends on the state's rules, which may tax the discounted price or the original price. Your order summary shows the figures that apply to your order. If you are close to a threshold or comparing totals, check the summary for each payment method.

## Wholesale buyers
Retailers have their own obligations, such as licenses, tax registration and stamps, which may differ from the rules for individuals. If you buy wholesale, check with your state's tax authority about what applies to your business, and see our [wholesale ordering guide](/blog/wholesale-ordering-guide/). We supply registered businesses, and they are responsible for compliance with their own tax rules.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Why does the tax differ between products?
Because states tax by price, by volume or by item, and some treat disposables, bottles and devices differently.

### Will you add tax to my order?
Where a tax applies to your order, it is itemized in your order total before you pay. If you have questions about how tax appears on your order, contact us with your state.

### Can I avoid vape tax?
Taxes are set by law, and a seller that follows the law cannot skip them. Be cautious of sellers that offer to avoid tax, because that may mean they are not complying with the rules, which can put your order at risk.

### Do taxes change often?
Yes. States change rates and methods from time to time. Check official sources before a large purchase.

### Does tax affect returns?
Refunds are based on what you paid for the returned item, and any tax paid on it is handled according to the rules that apply. We explain the details when we arrange a return. See [refund and return policy explained](/blog/refund-and-return-policy-explained/).

## Questions
Contact us through the [contact page](/contact/) with your state and we will explain how it appears on your order. Browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) and [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Frequently asked questions about tax on your order
### Why do two customers pay different tax for the same product?
Because tax depends on where the parcel is going. A product shipped to a state with a percentage tax carries more tax than one shipped to a state with none, and a state that taxes by the milliliter charges more on a large bottle.

### Is the tax part of the price I see on the product page?
The product page shows the price of the product. Where a tax applies to your order, it is itemized in your order summary, so you see the full amount before you pay.

### Do taxes apply to accessories and parts?
It depends on the state. Some tax devices and accessories as well as liquids, and some do not. If you are unsure, ask us with your state.

## Keeping records
If you are a business or you track your spending, keep your order confirmation and invoice, which show the items, the totals and any tax. For a retailer, these records support your own tax filings. For an individual, they are simply a record of what you paid. If you need an invoice in a particular format, ask us.

## Staying informed
State tax rules are updated through legislation and regulation, and the details are published by state revenue departments. If you buy regularly, check your state's page once or twice a year, and again when you hear of a change. Being aware of changes helps you plan larger orders and avoid surprises.

## A short checklist before a larger order
1. Find your state's rule on vapor products and note whether it taxes by price, volume or item.
2. Check your order summary for any tax line before you pay.
3. Compare totals for each payment method, including any discount.
4. Keep the invoice for your records.
5. Contact us with your state if a line on the summary is unclear.

Five minutes of checking is cheaper than a surprise at the end of the process.
